newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish accountants earn under 50,000 punts-survey.
newsitem.headline: Irish accountants earn under 50,000 punts-survey.

text.p: A typical chartered accountant in Ireland earns less than 49,000 Irish pounds per annum and chartered accountants in financial services are paid more that those in industry and commerce, a survey showed on Thursday.

The main factors determining salaries were the size of the company, position within the firm and the year of qualification, a new survey on chartered accountants' salaries published by the Leinster Society of Chartered Accountants (LSCA) showed.
The survey showed the head of finance employed in industry and commerce earning an average 52,200 punts while their counterpart in financial services earned 69,500 punts per year.
Tax managers and directors employed in the top six accountancy firms earn an average of 46,500 punts.
The survey covered 542 chartered accountants, 135 of whom were women.
"Because there are fewer women qualified more than 10 years, less are in senior positions compared to men," the LSCA said.
It said that while 31 percent of audit seniors were women, only 16 percent of head of finance category were women and there were no women among the 26 managing directors.

The survey showed that an increase in the taxation on company cars to 30 percent from 20 percent appeared to reduce the numbers driving company cars to 41 percent from 57 percent between 1991 and 1997.
